title: Routing-free expert self-activation with functional Views
hypothesis: A shared expert basis plus per-expert Mirror coordinates can jointly specialize expert outputs and self-activation decisions without a centralized top-k router, using fewer bytes than independent routing-free experts.
physical_object: one shared expert transform and one shared activation prototype family
mirror_coordinate: per-expert coefficient jointly modulating output matrix and self-activation centroid
logical_multiplicity: four logical experts with self-activation over four token modes
controls: central top-1 router with independent experts
native low-rank output and activation-coordinate control

development.selection_metric: mode routing accuracy, output nRMSE, load balance, payload bytes and active compute

fresh.reason: native low-rank output/prototype control is checked before fresh access

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Routing-free Mirror achieves mode accuracy >=.95, output nRMSE <=.02, balanced loads, >=25% fewer bytes than independent routing-free experts, and beats native coordinate controls at matched compute.
failure_gate: FAIL if self-activation loses balance/quality, byte/compute gates miss, or native coordinate controls exactly alias Mirror.
boundaries: Synthetic Gaussian modes and linear experts; no trained routing-free MoE or LM loss claim.
Self-activation uses expert-local scores and adaptive balance offsets, not centralized top-k logits.
No learned gating or SGD in this screen; coordinates are oracle-estimated from generated operators.
